title: PostgreSQL 18 Tutorial (Part I)
why: Hands-on first CREATE/INSERT/SELECT trace, join and aggregate walkthroughs, and a short transaction tutorial that match the early SQLite/PostgreSQL sandbox labs.

title: PostgreSQL 18, Part II: The SQL Language
why: Authoritative reference for value types and casts, DDL constraints and foreign keys, joins, aggregates, subqueries, CTEs, window functions and NULL expression semantics.

title: SQL As Understood by SQLite
why: Syntax reference for the SQLite CLI and Python stdlib labs, covering SELECT, joins, aggregates, WITH clauses, window functions and transactions.

title: Database System Concepts, 7th edition: author's slides
version: 7th edition slide index, chapter decks updated Jan-Mar 2019 (index read 2026-10-19)
why: Free author decks for every chapter, including ch. 7 Relational Database Design (functional dependencies, 3NF) and ch. 17 Transactions and ch. 18 Concurrency Control (two-phase locking).

title: Go standard library: database/sql
why: Authoritative reference for DB/Tx/Rows/Stmt ownership, connection pooling, context cancellation and error handling in Go database clients.

title: Avoiding SQL injection risk (Go documentation)
why: Shows the parameter-binding boundary that prevents injection and the unsafe fmt.Sprintf string-assembly alternative.

title: pgx: PostgreSQL driver and toolkit for Go (v5)
why: Pinned driver documentation for the later Go labs: connection configuration and pooling, prepared statements, transactions and row scanning.

title: Database System Concepts
why: Canonical textbook treatment of functional dependencies, normalization to third normal form, schema design and ACID transaction foundations.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation, Chapter 66: Database Physical Storage
why: Official description of how tables and indexes become files of fixed-size pages, with item identifiers, free space, and the free-space and visibility maps a real engine maintains.

title: SQLite Database File Format
version: SQLite 3 on-disk format (all releases since 3.0.0); page read 2026-10-19
why: Byte-level specification of pages, b-tree interior and leaf cells, cell pointer arrays, freeblocks and overflow pages, ideal for tracing a lookup through real page bytes in the sandbox.

title: Architecture of a Database System
version: Foundations and Trends in Databases 1(2), 2007, pp. 141-259
why: The standard architecture survey: buffer-pool frames, pin counts, dirty pages and replacement, heap versus B+-tree access methods and row IDs, the iterator model, and selectivity estimation.

title: Query Evaluation Techniques for Large Databases
version: ACM Computing Surveys 25(2), June 1993, pp. 73-170; revision dated 1993-11-10
why: Definitive treatment of operator trees and iterators, nested-loop, sort-merge and hash joins, sorting and grouping, and the memory limits that force spilling to disk.

title: The Log-Structured Merge-Tree (LSM-Tree)
why: Original LSM design: memory-resident C0 tree, disk C1 tree, rolling merges, deferred deletes and the multi-component cost argument.

title: RocksDB Wiki: Compaction
version: RocksDB wiki page, last edited 2023-06-29 (41 revisions)
why: Official account of leveled, tiered and hybrid compaction, sorted runs, and the read/write/space amplification trade-offs that explain why an LSM engine rewrites data.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation, 14.1: Using EXPLAIN
why: How to read a plan tree: sequential, index, bitmap and index-only scans, join node choices, cost and row estimates, and EXPLAIN ANALYZE actual rows and timings.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation, 14.2: Statistics Used by the Planner
why: Concrete bridge from stored data to selectivity: reltuples/relpages, most-common values, histogram bounds, n_distinct, correlation, and why correlated columns defeat the independence assumption.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: Reliability and the Write-Ahead Log
why: Primary account of PostgreSQL's WAL, checkpointing and crash recovery, to contrast with SQLite's rollback-journal and WAL designs.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: Concurrency Control
why: Official chapter on MVCC and snapshot visibility whose sub-pages give the READ COMMITTED/REPEATABLE READ/SERIALIZABLE guarantees, explicit row locks and deadlock handling.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: Routine Vacuuming
why: Definitive description of dead tuples, old-version retention, long transactions, transaction ID wraparound and autovacuum for the MVCC cleanup chapter.

title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
why: SQLite's own account of its rollback-journal commit protocol, sector-write and ordering assumptions, and hot-journal recovery.

title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
why: How SQLite's WAL mode actually works: checkpoints, snapshots, reader/writer interaction, and the WAL-reset corruption bug and its fix.

title: Isolation In SQLite
why: Short authoritative statement of SQLite's actual isolation behaviour and read transactions in rollback-journal and WAL modes.

title: ARIES: A Transaction Recovery Method Supporting Fine-Granularity Locking and Partial Rollbacks Using Write-Ahead Logging
version: ACM Transactions on Database Systems 17(1), March 1992, pp. 94-162
why: The original ARIES paper: redo/undo logging, LSNs, the analysis/redo/undo restart phases, and fuzzy checkpoints.

title: Serializable Snapshot Isolation in PostgreSQL
why: Design and implementation of PostgreSQL's SERIALIZABLE level, covering write-skew detection, dangerous structures and serialization failures.

title: PostgreSQL 18: ALTER TABLE
why: Reference for each ALTER TABLE subform's lock level, NOT VALID plus VALIDATE CONSTRAINT for non-blocking constraint checks, and ATTACH/DETACH PARTITION lock behaviour.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Monitoring Database Activity
why: Chapter entry point to the cumulative statistics system, pg_stat_activity and related views, lock inspection, and progress reporting, with EXPLAIN cross-referenced for single-query analysis.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Backup and Restore
why: Contrasts SQL dumps, file-system-level backups and continuous archiving, and introduces base backups plus archived WAL for point-in-time recovery.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Privileges
why: Explains object ownership, GRANT/REVOKE, grant options, PUBLIC defaults, and role-based least privilege for application accounts.

title: PostgreSQL 18: High Availability, Load Balancing, and Replication
why: Primary account of log-shipping and streaming standbys, synchronous versus asynchronous commit, failover, and the stale-read tradeoff of hot standbys.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Table Partitioning
why: Declarative range, list and hash partitioning, partition pruning, and the maintenance and planning tradeoffs that separate local partitions from independent shards.

title: PostgreSQL 18: PREPARE TRANSACTION
why: Concrete two-phase commit mechanics: the prepared on-disk state, COMMIT/ROLLBACK PREPARED from another session, pg_prepared_xacts, and the danger of forgotten in-doubt transactions.

title: DuckDB: an Embeddable Analytical Database
why: Original description of an in-process analytical engine with columnar compressed blocks, vectorized execution, and an explicit comparison against a row-oriented transactional baseline.

title: SQLite: Datatypes In SQLite
why: Defines SQLite's storage classes, column affinity rules and the DECIMAL-to-NUMERIC affinity example needed to show that a declared type does not fix storage.

title: SQLite: SELECT
why: Documents the illustrative FROM/WHERE/result/DISTINCT steps, the warning that they are not an execution order, and DISTINCT's NULL and result-row comparison rules.

title: SQLite: Expressions
why: Primary SQLite syntax for single-quoted string constants and CAST, including the longest-prefix rule for TEXT to INTEGER.

title: SQLite grammar: src/parse.y
why: Pinned grammar showing that a SELECT result column accepts an alias with AS, as a bare identifier, or not at all.

title: PostgreSQL 18: SELECT
why: Authoritative PostgreSQL statement of default duplicate retention, DISTINCT semantics, and AS output names.

title: PostgreSQL 18: Lexical Structure
why: Defines PostgreSQL string constants bounded by single quotes and the doubled-quote escape.

title: PostgreSQL 18: integer text conversion (numutils.c)
why: Pinned C source for the 32-bit integer parser used by text-to-integer input, including its error on bad input format and trailing characters.

title: PostgreSQL 18: int4in (int.c)
why: Pinned text-input function int4in, which converts a string to a 32-bit integer by calling pg_strtoint32_safe.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation, 9.2: Comparison Functions and Operators
why: Documents ordinary comparison results with NULL, IS DISTINCT FROM, and the IS NULL / IS NOT NULL tests.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation, 9.1: Logical Operators
why: Complete three-valued AND, OR and NOT truth tables for SQL conditions.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation, 4.2.14: Expression Evaluation Rules
why: Official caveat that subexpression evaluation order is undefined and operands need not be evaluated left-to-right.

title: NULL Handling in SQLite Versus Other Database Engines
why: SQLite's own comparison chart of NULL arithmetic and Boolean behaviour across engines; the underlying tests date from 2002.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: Date/Time Types
why: Definitive statement of timestamp with/without time zone storage, offset interpretation, and session-zone display.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation: Collation Support
why: Explains that PostgreSQL text ordering comes from the expression's collation and that the default is the database-creation locale.

title: SQLite: Date And Time Functions
why: Documents accepted time-value formats and the exact treatment of Z and numeric timezone offsets used by the time lab.

title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
why: Standards definition of the Z designator and of numeric offsets as local time minus UTC.

title: SQLite: Floating Point Numbers
why: SQLite's own account of its 64-bit two's-complement integers and its IEEE 754 binary-64 REAL storage, including the 47.49 price and cents examples behind the integer-cent and 0.1 + 0.2 discussion.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation, 8.1: Numeric Types
why: Primary reference for bigint range and out-of-range errors, numeric precision and scale, declared-scale rounding and precision overflow, and the documented inexactness of real and double precision.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation, 9.3: Mathematical Functions and Operators
why: Table 9.4 documents / returning the same type as its arguments and truncating towards zero for the integral types.

title: PostgreSQL source: src/backend/utils/adt/int8.c
why: Pinned implementation showing that bigint +, - and * check for 64-bit overflow and raise the error "bigint out of range" instead of wrapping.

title: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation, 7.3: Select Lists
why: States that DISTINCT compares all column values of result rows and treats nulls as equal for duplicate elimination.
